claim: PglC is a full-length monotopic membrane protein with phosphoglycosyl transferase (PGT) activity.
source: Recently, we reported the X-ray structure determination of PglC, a full-length monotopic membrane protein with phosphoglycosyl transferase (PGT) activity.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a previously reported finding.

claim: Two motifs in PglC exemplify principles of topology determination that can be applied to the identification of reentrant domains among diverse monotopic proteins.
source: Using the new information gained from studies on the PGT superfamily we demonstrate that two motifs exemplify principles of topology determination that can be applied to the identification of reentrant domains among diverse monotopic proteins of interest.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract and demonstrated through the LpxM analysis in the manuscript.

claim: Monotopic membrane proteins integrate into the lipid bilayer via reentrant hydrophobic domains that enter and exit on a single face of the membrane.
source: Monotopic membrane proteins integrate into the lipid bilayer via reentrant hydrophobic domains that enter and exit on a single face of the membrane.
evidence: This is a definitional statement based on established scientific knowledge about monotopic membrane proteins.

claim: Current bioinformatics approaches enable relatively reliable prediction of transmembrane helix topology in polytopic and bitopic membrane proteins.
source: Current bioinformatics approaches (Elazar et al., 2016; Krogh et al., 2001; Tsirigos et al., 2015) enable a relatively reliable prediction of transmembrane helix topology in polytopic and bitopic membrane proteins on the basis of hydrophobicity, homology with known protein structures, and the 'positive-inside rule', by which membrane proteins have been empirically determined to preferentially adopt topologies that position positively charged residues at the cytoplasmic face of the membrane (Gafvelin and von Heijne, 1994; Heijne, 1986; von Heijne, 2006), among other parameters.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published bioinformatics methods and empirical observations.

claim: Current knowledge of monotopic topologies is relatively limited.
source: By comparison, current knowledge of monotopic topologies is relatively limited.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The key determinants that distinguish reentrant domains in monotopic proteins from transmembrane helices in bitopic proteins are poorly understood.
source: In particular, the key determinants that distinguish reentrant domains in monotopic proteins from transmembrane helices in bitopic proteins, to result in the two distinct topologies, are poorly understood.
evidence: This statement describes a gap in current scientific understanding.

claim: PGTs are integral membrane proteins that initiate glycoconjugate biosynthesis pathways by catalyzing the transfer of a phosphosugar from a sugar nucleoside diphosphate donor to a membrane-resident polyprenol phosphate.
source: PGTs are integral membrane proteins that initiate a wide variety of essential glycoconjugate biosynthesis pathways, including peptidoglycan and N-linked glycan biosynthesis, by catalyzing the transfer of a phosphosugar from a sugar nucleoside diphosphate donor to a membrane-resident polyprenol phosphate.
evidence: This describes the biochemical function of PGTs based on established knowledge.

claim: PGTs can be grouped into two superfamilies based on their membrane topology.
source: PGTs can be grouped broadly into two superfamilies based on their membrane topology (Lukose et al., 2017).
evidence: This classification is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: One PGT superfamily is composed of polytopic PGTs with 10- and 11- transmembrane helices, exemplified by bacterial MraY and WecA.
source: One superfamily, exemplified by bacterial MraY and WecA, is composed of polytopic PGTs with 10- and 11- transmembrane helices respectively and active sites crafted from extended cytoplasmic inter-TM loops (Anderson et al., 2000).
evidence: This structural characterization is supported by a citation.

claim: The eukaryotic PGT Alg7 belongs to the polytopic PGT superfamily.
source: The eukaryotic PGT Alg7, which initiates the dolichol pathway for N-linked protein glycosylation, belongs to this superfamily (Burda and Aebi, 1999).
evidence: This classification is supported by a citation.

claim: A second PGT superfamily is exemplified by the monotopic enzyme PglC from Campylobacter jejuni.
source: A second superfamily is exemplified by the monotopic enzyme, PglC, from the Gram-negative bacterium Campylobacter jejuni (Glover et al., 2006; Szymanski et al., 1999).
evidence: This classification is supported by citations.

claim: The monotopic PGT superfamily shares a common functional core comprising a single N-terminal membrane-inserted domain and a small globular domain.
source: The PGTs in this superfamily share a common functional core, which is homologous to PglC and comprises a single N-terminal membrane-inserted domain and a small globular domain (Lukose et al., 2015).
evidence: This structural description is supported by a citation.

claim: Topology predictions suggested that the N-terminal hydrophobic domain of PglC forms a transmembrane helix with the N-terminus in the periplasm and the globular domain in the cytoplasm.
source: Topology predictions using multiple algorithms suggested that the N-terminal hydrophobic domain of PglC, and the analogous domain in other superfamily members, forms a transmembrane helix, such that the N-terminus is in the periplasm and the globular domain in the cytoplasm (Furlong et al., 2015; Lukose et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes predictions from computational algorithms, supported by citations.

claim: Biochemical analysis of WcaJ supported a reentrant topology model rather than a membrane-spanning one.
source: However, biochemical analysis of WcaJ, a WbaP homolog, supported a model wherein both termini of the corresponding domain of WcaJ are in the cytoplasm, forming a reentrant topology, rather than a membrane-spanning one (Furlong et al., 2015).
evidence: This experimental finding is supported by a citation.

claim: The X-ray structure of PglC from Campylobacter concisus was determined to a resolution of 2.7 Å.
source: Recently, we reported the X-ray structure of PglC from Campylobacter concisus to a resolution of 2.7 Å (PDB 5W7L) (Ray et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the reported structure with citation.

claim: PglC from C. concisus and C. jejuni share 72% sequence identity.
source: The structural analysis complements previous biochemical studies on PglC from C. jejuni; the homologs share 72% sequence identity.
evidence: This is a quantitative statement about sequence similarity.

claim: In the reported structure, the N-terminal domain of PglC forms a reentrant helix-break-helix structure termed the reentrant membrane helix (RMH).
source: In the reported structure, the N-terminal domain of PglC forms a reentrant helix-break-helix structure, termed the reentrant membrane helix (RMH), such that both the N-terminus and the globular domain, which includes the active site, are on the cytoplasmic face of the inner membrane (Figure 1A).
evidence: This structural description is supported by the crystal structure and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Both the N-terminus and the globular domain of PglC are on the cytoplasmic face of the inner membrane.
source: In the reported structure, the N-terminal domain of PglC forms a reentrant helix-break-helix structure, termed the reentrant membrane helix (RMH), such that both the N-terminus and the globular domain, which includes the active site, are on the cytoplasmic face of the inner membrane (Figure 1A).
evidence: This topological feature is described in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: A reentrant topology for PglC was confirmed in vivo using a substituted cysteine accessibility method (SCAM).
source: A reentrant topology was further confirmed in vivo using a substituted cysteine accessibility method (SCAM) (Nasie et al., 2013; Ray et al., 2018).
evidence: This experimental confirmation is supported by citations.

claim: The same reentrant topology is confirmed in both PglC and the corresponding domain of WbaP homolog WcaJ.
source: As such, the same reentrant topology is confirmed in both PglC and the corresponding domain of an elaborated WbaP homolog, suggesting that the topology and mechanism of membrane association enforced by the RMH is a conserved feature of the PGTs in this extensive superfamily.
evidence: This comparative statement is based on experimental data from both proteins.

claim: The topology and mechanism of membrane association enforced by the RMH is a conserved feature of the monotopic PGT superfamily.
source: As such, the same reentrant topology is confirmed in both PglC and the corresponding domain of an elaborated WbaP homolog, suggesting that the topology and mechanism of membrane association enforced by the RMH is a conserved feature of the PGTs in this extensive superfamily.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of similar topology in multiple superfamily members.

claim: The RMH is composed of an α-helix broken at a 118° angle by a conserved Ser23-Pro24 dyad.
source: The RMH is composed of an α-helix broken at a 118° angle by a conserved Ser23-Pro24 dyad (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This structural feature is described in the text and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Pro24 disrupts the hydrogen-bonding network of the RMH backbone, creating a break in the helix.
source: In the reported structure, Pro24 disrupts the hydrogen-bonding network of the RMH backbone, creating a break in the helix.
evidence: This structural observation is based on the crystal structure.

claim: The Ser23 side chain forms a 2.6 Å hydrogen bond with the backbone carbonyl of Ile20.
source: This break is stabilized in turn by the orientation of the Ser23 side chain, which forms a 2.6 Å hydrogen bond with the backbone carbonyl of Ile20, thus satisfying one of the backbone hydrogen bonds lost due to Pro24.
evidence: This is a specific structural measurement from the crystal structure.

claim: Pro24 is highly conserved among PglC homologs.
source: Pro24 is highly conserved among PglC homologs, and has been previously shown to be important for PglC activity (Lukose et al., 2015).
evidence: This conservation is observed in sequence analysis and the functional importance is cited.

claim: Pro24 has been previously shown to be important for PglC activity.
source: Pro24 is highly conserved among PglC homologs, and has been previously shown to be important for PglC activity (Lukose et al., 2015).
evidence: This functional importance is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Lys7 makes short-range contacts with Asp169 at the C-terminus of the globular domain.
source: At the N-terminus of PglC there is a similarly conserved Lys7-Arg8 dyad. Lys7 makes short-range contacts with the C-terminus of the globular domain via residue Asp169, and Arg8 interacts with the headgroup of a co-purified phospholipid molecule (Figure 1D).
evidence: This structural interaction is observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Arg8 interacts with the headgroup of a co-purified phospholipid molecule.
source: At the N-terminus of PglC there is a similarly conserved Lys7-Arg8 dyad. Lys7 makes short-range contacts with the C-terminus of the globular domain via residue Asp169, and Arg8 interacts with the headgroup of a co-purified phospholipid molecule (Figure 1D).
evidence: This interaction is observed in the crystal structure and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: PglC is currently the only example of a structurally-characterized monotopic membrane protein that associates with the membrane via a highly-ordered, reentrant helix-break-helix motif that penetrates into the hydrophobic membrane core.
source: However, PglC is currently the only example of a structurally-characterized monotopic membrane protein that associates with the membrane via a highly-ordered, reentrant helix-break-helix motif that penetrates into the hydrophobic membrane core.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about the uniqueness of PglC among structurally characterized proteins.

claim: Current membrane topology prediction algorithms typically default to the assumption that hydrophobic α-helices of a certain length range are membrane-spanning.
source: Current membrane topology prediction algorithms typically default to the assumption that hydrophobic α-helices of a certain length range are membrane-spanning (Elazar et al., 2016; Krogh et al., 2001; Tsirigos et al., 2015), making the specific prediction of monotopic topologies with reentrant α-helices challenging.
evidence: This describes a limitation of current computational methods, supported by citations.

claim: The reported structure of PglC is stable in a membrane environment over 400 ns of MD simulations.
source: Over 400 ns of simulation time, RMSD values within ~1 Å were measured for PglC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1). These analyses support that the conformation of PglC observed in the crystal structure reflects a native state in a lipid bilayer environment.
evidence: This stability is demonstrated by MD simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The conformation of PglC observed in the crystal structure reflects a native state in a lipid bilayer environment.
source: Over 400 ns of simulation time, RMSD values within ~1 Å were measured for PglC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1). These analyses support that the conformation of PglC observed in the crystal structure reflects a native state in a lipid bilayer environment.
evidence: This conclusion is based on MD simulation data.

claim: S23A and P24A PglC variants form reentrant topologies with both termini in the cytoplasm.
source: In the current study, the same cysteine substitutions were used in SCAM analyses to determine the topology of S23A and P24A PglC variants. Similar to wild-type PglC, both variants were found to form reentrant topologies with both termini in the cytoplasm (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by SCAM analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In the S23A/P24A PglC variant, all four cysteines were significantly protected from PEGylation by both NEM and MTSES, suggesting all four cysteines were in the periplasm.
source: However, in a S23A/P24A PglC variant, all four cysteines were significantly protected from PEGylation by both NEM and MTSES, suggesting that all four cysteines were in the periplasm.
evidence: This is based on SCAM analysis data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The folding of S23A/P24A PglC is substantially perturbed by mutation of the Ser-Pro dyad to Ala-Ala.
source: Although the precise nature of the S23A/P24A PglC topology cannot be determined from these data, it is clear that the folding of this variant is substantially perturbed by mutation of the Ser-Pro dyad to Ala-Ala.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the aberrant SCAM results for the double mutant.

claim: Ser23 and Pro24 act synergistically to establish a reentrant topology that positions both the N- and C-terminus of PglC in the cytoplasm.
source: These results suggest that Ser23 and Pro24 act synergistically to establish a reentrant topology that positions both the N- and C-terminus of PglC in the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of single and double mutant SCAM results.

claim: During MD simulations, the break in the RMH is maintained by hydrogen bonding alternately between the side chain hydroxyl group and backbone amide of Ser23 and the backbone carbonyls of Leu19 and Ile20.
source: Indeed, in simulations of PglC performed in a POPE membrane, it was observed that the break imposed by the Ser-Pro motif is additionally maintained by hydrogen bonding alternately between the side chain hydroxyl group and backbone amide of Ser23 and the backbone carbonyls of Leu19 and Ile20 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This dynamic behavior is observed in MD simulations and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The break in the RMH is stabilized by an extensive network of dynamic hydrogen bonds between Leu19, Ile20 and Ser23.
source: This suggests that the break in the RMH is stabilized by an extensive network of dynamic hydrogen bonds between Leu19, Ile20 and Ser23 that compensate for the absence of a hydrogen-bond donor in Pro24 and enforce a helix-break-helix topology.
evidence: This is inferred from the MD simulation observations.

claim: In the peptide corresponding to wild-type PglC, residues Leu19 through Pro24 remained mostly unstructured during folding simulations, while the N-terminus and the sequence following the Ser-Pro motif rapidly adopted an α-helical conformation.
source: Significant differences in folding behavior between the two peptides were observed over the full 1.6 µs of simulation time; in the peptide corresponding to wild-type PglC, residues Leu19 through Pro24, encompassing the Ser-Pro motif and surrounding hydrogen bonds, remained mostly unstructured, while the N-terminus and the sequence following the Ser-Pro motif rapidly adopted an α-helical conformation (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This folding behavior is observed in MD simulations shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the peptide corresponding to S23A/P24A PglC, residues Leu19 through Ile33 folded into a continuous α-helix during folding simulations.
source: In contrast, in the peptide corresponding to S23A/P24A PglC, residues Leu19 through Ile33 folded into a continuous α-helix, and this secondary structure appeared much later in the folding process.
evidence: This folding behavior is observed in MD simulations shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The Ser-Pro motif drives formation of the helix-break-helix structure observed in the RMH of wild-type PglC.
source: These simulations indicate that the Ser-Pro motif drives formation of the helix-break-helix structure observed in the RMH of wild-type PglC, while the corresponding domain of S23A/P24A PglC has an intrinsic tendency to form a single, uninterrupted helix.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the comparison of folding simulations.

claim: The corresponding domain of S23A/P24A PglC has an intrinsic tendency to form a single, uninterrupted helix.
source: These simulations indicate that the Ser-Pro motif drives formation of the helix-break-helix structure observed in the RMH of wild-type PglC, while the corresponding domain of S23A/P24A PglC has an intrinsic tendency to form a single, uninterrupted helix.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the folding simulation results.

claim: The Ser-Pro motif facilitates proper folding and membrane insertion of the N-terminal domain in a reentrant topology during an early co-translational folding event.
source: The difference in the simulated folding of the two peptides underscores the significance of the Ser-Pro motif for RMH formation, and further supports a model by which this motif facilitates proper folding and membrane insertion of the N-terminal domain in a reentrant topology during an early co-translational folding event.
evidence: This is a mechanistic model inferred from the folding simulation results.

claim: S23A/P24A SUMO-PglC has a Tm of 42.6 ± 2.0 °C.
source: It was found that the S23A/P24A SUMO-PglC variant, with a Tm of 42.6 ± 2.0 °C, is significantly less stable relative to wild-type SUMO-PglC, which had a Tm of 49.9 ± 1.5 °C (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from thermal shift assays shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Wild-type SUMO-PglC has a Tm of 49.9 ± 1.5 °C.
source: It was found that the S23A/P24A SUMO-PglC variant, with a Tm of 42.6 ± 2.0 °C, is significantly less stable relative to wild-type SUMO-PglC, which had a Tm of 49.9 ± 1.5 °C (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from thermal shift assays shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The ΔTm of 7.3 ± 2.5 °C between wild-type and S23A/P24A SUMO-PglC indicates a loss in thermal stability upon mutation of the Ser-Pro motif to Ala-Ala.
source: The ΔTm of 7.3 ± 2.5 °C between the wild-type and S23A/P24A SUMO-PglC indicates a loss in thermal stability upon mutation of the Ser-Pro motif to Ala-Ala.
evidence: This is calculated from the thermal shift assay data.

claim: The Ser-Pro motif is necessary for formation of the RMH domain and has a strong influence on the stability of the entire PglC structure.
source: Thus, the Ser-Pro motif is not only necessary for formation of the RMH domain, but additionally has a strong influence on the stability of the entire PglC structure.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the thermal stability and MD simulation data.

claim: In S23A/P24A PglC, the interior of the protein containing the putative polyprenol phosphate binding site appeared to collapse during MD simulations.
source: Whereas wild-type PglC was stable over 400 ns of simulations in a POPE membrane, the interior of S23A/P24A PglC, containing the putative polyprenol phosphate binding site proximal to the active site, appeared to collapse.
evidence: This structural change is observed in MD simulations shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In S23A/P24A PglC, the positions of residues Leu21, Leu90 and Val180 moved closer to each other over 400 ns of MD simulations, significantly reducing the volume of the protein interior.
source: Specifically, in S23A/P24A PglC, the positions of residues Leu21 on the RMH, and of Leu90 and Val180 on two amphipathic helices at the membrane interface, were all found to move closer to each other over the course of 400 ns, significantly reducing the volume of the protein interior (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is observed in MD simulations and shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The Ser-Pro motif plays an important role in maintaining the RMH and the associated amphipathic helices in the correct conformation in the PglC fold.
source: The collapse of the S23A/P24A PglC tertiary structure upon substitution of the Ser-Pro motif suggests that the motif plays an important role not only in forming the RMH, but also in maintaining the RMH and the associated amphipathic helices in the correct conformation in the PglC fold.
evidence: This is inferred from the MD simulation observations of structural collapse.

claim: The collapse of the S23A/P24A PglC fold appeared to hinder the passage of lipids into the interior of the fold relative to wild-type PglC.
source: Additionally, it was observed that the collapse of the S23A/P24A PglC fold appeared to hinder the passage of lipids into the interior of the fold relative to wild-type PglC.
evidence: This is observed in MD simulations shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: Mutation of either Lys7 or Arg8 to Ala did not have a significant effect on the final topology of PglC.
source: Mutation of either Lys7 or Arg8 to Ala did not have a significant effect on the final topology of PglC.
evidence: This is demonstrated by SCAM analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: In the K7A/R8A PglC variant, the N-terminus became partially localized to the periplasm.
source: However, when both conserved residues were mutated in the K7A/R8A PglC variant, it was observed that the N-terminus (represented by K4C and F6C) became partially localized to the periplasm.
evidence: This is demonstrated by SCAM analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: The K7A/R8A PglC population was split between proteins adopting the native reentrant topology and those adopting a non-native membrane-spanning topology.
source: This suggested that the K7A/R8A PglC population was split between proteins adopting the native reentrant topology, in which the N-terminus is in the cytoplasm, and those adopting a non-native membrane-spanning topology.
evidence: This is inferred from the SCAM analysis results.

claim: A K7A/R8A/P24A PglC variant adopted the same non-native, all-periplasmic topology previously observed for S23A/P24A PglC.
source: Notably, a K7A/R8A/P24A PglC variant adopted the same non-native, all-periplasmic topology previously observed for S23A/P24A PglC, suggesting that, as with S23A/P24A PglC, the native folding process of the RMH had been significantly perturbed.
evidence: This is demonstrated by SCAM analysis shown in Figure 5.

claim: The positively charged Lys-Arg motif and the helix-breaking Ser-Pro motif act cooperatively to enforce a reentrant topology for PglC.
source: Taken together, these analyses indicate that the positively charged Lys-Arg motif and the helix-breaking Ser-Pro motif act cooperatively to enforce a reentrant topology for PglC.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the combined SCAM analysis results of various mutants.

claim: The inter-helical angle of the RMH in the PglC structure is 118°.
source: While the in vivo SCAM analyses and MD simulations are consistent with the reported structure of PglC, we noted that the inter-helical angle of the RMH in the structure (118°) (Figure 1A) is significantly more open than that observed in the peptide modeling (Figure 3B) and in reentrant helices found in reported polytopic membrane protein structures (Viklund et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a structural measurement from the crystal structure.

claim: In the E3C/I163C SUMO-PglC variant, the two cysteines at positions Glu3 and Ile163 have a Cβ-Cβ distance of ~5.2 Å in the PglC fold.
source: If the reported structure reflects a native conformation of the RMH, the two residues at these positions have a Cβ-Cβ distance of ~5.2 Å in the PglC fold (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a distance measurement from the crystal structure shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The two cysteines in E3C/I163C SUMO-PglC could be crosslinked with dibromobimane (bBBr).
source: Although oxidation to a disulfide was not observed, the two cysteines could be crosslinked in the E3C/I163C SUMO-PglC variant with dibromobimane (bBBr), a short, bifunctional thiol-specific labeling reagent.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the crosslinking experiments shown in Figure 6B.

claim: bBBr-treated E3C/I163C SUMO-PglC was significantly more fluorescent than either single cysteine variants or a control variant with two cysteines too far apart for crosslinking.
source: Indeed, bBBr-treated E3C/I163C SUMO-PglC was significantly more fluorescent than were either single cysteine variants (E3C SUMO-PglC and I163C SUMO-PglC), or a control variant (E3C/S88C SUMO-PglC) with two cysteine residues too far apart for crosslinking by bBBr (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by fluorescence measurements shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The extended RMH observed in the crystal structure reflects a native conformation of the PglC fold.
source: These crosslinking studies suggest that the extended RMH observed in the crystal structure reflects a native conformation of the PglC fold.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the crosslinking data.

claim: The distance between Arg3 and Leu164 remains invariable over 400 ns of MD simulations of PglC in a POPE membrane.
source: In simulations of PglC in a POPE membrane it was observed that the distance between these two residue positions remains invariable over 400 ns (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is observed in MD simulations shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The RMH is constrained in the position observed in the crystal structure, with little conformational freedom of the N-terminus relative to the globular domain.
source: This supports a model of PglC in which the RMH is constrained in the position observed in the crystal structure, with little conformational freedom of the N-terminus relative to the globular domain.
evidence: This is inferred from the MD simulation data showing invariable distance.

claim: Intramolecular crosslinking of E3C/I163C SUMO-PglC by bBBr did not impact catalytic activity.
source: Importantly, it was found that intramolecular crosslinking of E3C/I163C SUMO-PglC by bBBr did not impact catalytic activity (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is demonstrated by activity assays shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The crosslinked conformation of the RMH domain is compatible with catalysis.
source: This indicates that the crosslinked conformation of the RMH domain, which places the N-terminus in close proximity to the globular domain, is compatible with catalysis.
evidence: This is inferred from the activity data showing no loss of activity upon crosslinking.

claim: LpxM, LpxL and LpxP catalyze the transfer of myristoyl, lauroyl, or palmitoyl groups, respectively, to Kdo2-lipid IV to produce lipid A.
source: Three candidates – LpxM, LpxL and LpxP – are of particular interest. These enzymes catalyze the transfer of myristoyl, lauroyl, or palmitoyl groups, respectively, to Kdo2-lipid IV to produce lipid A, the lipidic component of outer membrane lipopolysaccharide found in most Gram-negative bacteria; as such, they carry significant therapeutic relevance as antibiotic targets.
evidence: This describes the biochemical function of these enzymes based on established knowledge.

claim: LpxM, LpxL and LpxP belong to a large family of lipid A biosynthesis acyltransferases with over 4000 homologs each.
source: LpxM, LpxL and LpxP belong to a large family of lipid A biosynthesis acyltransferases: over 4000 homologs of each sequence were identified during covariance analyses.
evidence: This is based on covariance analysis performed in the study.

claim: The biochemical function of LpxM, LpxL and LpxP dictates that the soluble C-terminal domain of each must localize to the cytoplasmic face of the inner membrane.
source: Additionally, the three enzymes belong to an extensive and diverse superfamily of lysophosphopholipid acyltransferases, which comprises members from all three domains of life and also includes several families of enzymes involved in triglyceride biosynthesis (Shi and Cheng, 2009; Takeuchi and Reue, 2009). The biochemical function of these enzymes in lipid A biosynthesis dictates that the soluble C-terminal domain of each must localize to the cytoplasmic face of the inner membrane; thus, the predicted transmembrane topology places the N-terminus in the periplasm.
evidence: This is inferred from the biochemical function and substrate location.

claim: Multiple positively-charged residues precede the hydrophobic domain in LpxM, LpxL and LpxP sequences.
source: However, we noted that multiple positively-charged residues precede the hydrophobic domain in each sequence, making localization of the N-terminus to the periplasm less likely.
evidence: This is observed in sequence analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: The hydrophobic domains of LpxM, LpxL and LpxP contain polar (Gln, Thr) and multiple aromatic (Trp, Tyr) residues not typically found in the middle of transmembrane helices.
source: In addition, the three hydrophobic domains contain polar (Gln, Thr) and multiple aromatic (Trp, Tyr) residues not typically found in the middle of transmembrane helices (von Heijne, 2006), as well as helix-breaking Pro and Gly residues.
evidence: This is observed in sequence analysis and compared to known properties of transmembrane helices.

claim: Covariance analyses of LpxM, LpxL and LpxP identified several instances of covariance between residues in the hydrophobic and globular domains.
source: Finally, covariance analyses of LpxM, LpxL and LpxP identified several instances of covariance between residues in the hydrophobic and globular domains (Supplementary file 4), suggesting interactions between the two.
evidence: This is based on covariance analysis performed in the study.

claim: SCAM analysis of LpxM revealed that both the N-terminus and the globular domain are located in the cytoplasm.
source: SCAM analysis of 'Cysless' LpxM and the six unique cysteine variants revealed that both the N-terminus and the globular domain of LpxM are located in the cytoplasm (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by SCAM analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: LpxM adopts a reentrant topology.
source: SCAM analysis of 'Cysless' LpxM and the six unique cysteine variants revealed that both the N-terminus and the globular domain of LpxM are located in the cytoplasm (Figure 7A). This confirms a reentrant topology for LpxM.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the SCAM analysis results.

claim: The reentrant topology is conserved among the related lipid A biosynthesis acyltransferases LpxM, LpxL and LpxP.
source: Given the similarity between LpxM, LpxL and LpxP, we propose that the reentrant topology is conserved among the related lipid A biosynthesis acyltransferases.
evidence: This is proposed based on sequence similarity and the experimental confirmation for LpxM.

claim: In the reported structure of LpxM from A. baumannii, the N-terminal domain protrudes from the globular domain as a helix-break-helix.
source: Notably, the only lipid A biosynthesis acyltransferase for which a structure has been reported to date is the LpxM homolog from Acinetobacter baumannii (Dovala et al., 2016). The N-terminus of the LpxM homolog from A. baumannii is similarly reported to be a predicted transmembrane domain; however, in the reported structure, this domain protrudes from the globular domain as a helix-break-helix (Figure 7B), reminiscent of a reentrant domain.
evidence: This structural observation is from the cited structure shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The hydrophobic region is shorter in LpxM from A. baumannii than in those from E. coli and other Gram-negative pathogens.
source: We also noted that the hydrophobic region is shorter in this homolog than in those from E. coli and other Gram-negative pathogens (Figure 7C), making a membrane-spanning topology particularly unlikely.
evidence: This is observed in sequence alignment shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The N-terminus of LpxM from A. baumannii forms a reentrant domain that penetrates the membrane more shallowly than the reentrant domains of LpxM homologs from E. coli and other bacteria.
source: On the contrary, this could indicate that the N-terminus of LpxM from A. baumannii forms a reentrant domain that penetrates the membrane more shallowly than the reentrant domains of LpxM homologs from E. coli and other bacteria.
evidence: This is inferred from the shorter hydrophobic region and structural observations.

claim: The RMH anchors PglC in the membrane.
source: The RMH domain is central to the structure and function of PglC; it anchors PglC in the membrane, interacts with several amphipathic helices to position the active site of PglC at the membrane-water interface, and mediates binding of the polyprenol phosphate substrate.
evidence: This functional role is described based on structural and functional data.

claim: The RMH interacts with several amphipathic helices to position the active site of PglC at the membrane-water interface.
source: The RMH domain is central to the structure and function of PglC; it anchors PglC in the membrane, interacts with several amphipathic helices to position the active site of PglC at the membrane-water interface, and mediates binding of the polyprenol phosphate substrate.
evidence: This functional role is described based on structural analysis.

claim: The RMH mediates binding of the polyprenol phosphate substrate.
source: The RMH domain is central to the structure and function of PglC; it anchors PglC in the membrane, interacts with several amphipathic helices to position the active site of PglC at the membrane-water interface, and mediates binding of the polyprenol phosphate substrate.
evidence: This functional role is inferred from structural and functional considerations.

claim: Four conserved residues (Lys7, Arg8, Ser23, Pro24) each make specific contributions both to the early formation of the RMH and to the stability of the final PglC fold.
source: In this study, we identify four conserved residues that each make specific contributions both to the early formation of the RMH and to the stability of the final PglC fold, creating a clear preference for a reentrant topology for PglC and facilitating PglC function.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Lys7 forms a salt bridge with Asp169 at the interface between the N-terminus and the globular domain.
source: In the reported structure of PglC, Lys7 forms a salt bridge with Asp169, a residue which is 98% conserved among PglC homologs, at the interface between the N-terminus and the globular domain (Figure 1D).
evidence: This structural interaction is observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Asp169 is 98% conserved among PglC homologs.
source: In the reported structure of PglC, Lys7 forms a salt bridge with Asp169, a residue which is 98% conserved among PglC homologs, at the interface between the N-terminus and the globular domain (Figure 1D).
evidence: This conservation is observed in sequence analysis.

claim: The corresponding Asp to Asp169 in the PglC homolog from C. jejuni was reported previously to be necessary for catalytic activity.
source: The corresponding Asp in the PglC homolog from C. jejuni was reported previously to be necessary for catalytic activity (Lukose et al., 2015).
evidence: This functional importance is supported by a citation.

claim: K7A SUMO-PglC was found to be catalytically inactive.
source: The K7A SUMO-PglC variant was similarly found to be catalytically inactive, despite adopting a reentrant topology, as were K7A/R8A and K7A/R8A/P24A SUMO-PglC (Figure 9).
evidence: This is demonstrated by activity assays shown in Figure 9.

claim: The salt bridge formed between Lys7 and Asp169 helps to constrain the N-terminus in close proximity to the globular domain and is necessary for catalytic activity.
source: This suggests that the salt bridge formed between Lys7 and Asp169 helps to constrain the N-terminus in close proximity to the globular domain, and that this interaction is necessary for catalytic activity.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data and the loss of activity in K7A mutant.

claim: R8A SUMO-PglC retained ~15% catalytic activity.
source: Unlike the inactive K7A SUMO-PglC variant, R8A SUMO-PglC was found to retain ~15% catalytic activity (Figure 9).
evidence: This is demonstrated by activity assays shown in Figure 9.

claim: Arg8 may play a less significant role in the PglC fold than does Lys7.
source: Thus, Arg8 may play a less significant role in the PglC fold than does Lys7.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of activity between K7A and R8A mutants.

claim: The network of hydrogen bonds enforced by the Ser-Pro motif acts as a rigidifying 'staple' at the break in the RMH to restrict the conformational freedom of this domain.
source: We propose that the network of hydrogen bonds enforced by the motif (Figure 1C and Figure 3A) acts as a rigidifying 'staple' at the break in the RMH to restrict the conformational freedom of this domain.
evidence: This is a mechanistic model proposed based on structural and MD simulation data.

claim: Pro24 is hypothesized to play an important role in binding to the polyprenol phosphate substrate.
source: As the only membrane-inserted domain in PglC, the RMH is likely responsible for binding to the polyprenol phosphate substrate in the membrane; Pro24 in particular is hypothesized to play an important role (Lukose et al., 2015).
evidence: This hypothesis is based on the location and properties of Pro24, with citation to previous work.

claim: Conserved prolines are found in polyisoprene recognition sequences in various enzymes.
source: Conserved prolines are found in polyisoprene recognition sequences in various enzymes (Zhou and Troy, 2003), and were previously proposed to contribute to polyprenol binding, possibly as a result of their disruption of peptide backbone hydrogen bonding (Zhou and Troy, 2005).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from cited literature.

claim: P24A SUMO-PglC was previously reported to be catalytically inactive.
source: Indeed, a P24A SUMO-PglC variant was previously reported to be catalytically inactive (Lukose et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: S23A SUMO-PglC exhibits near-wild type activity.
source: Notably, although both S23A and P24A SUMO-PglC variants retain native-like reentrant topologies, the S23A variant exhibits near-wild type activity, whereas the P24A and S23A/P24A variants are inactive (Figure 9).
evidence: This is demonstrated by activity assays shown in Figure 9.

claim: P24A and S23A/P24A SUMO-PglC variants are inactive.
source: Notably, although both S23A and P24A SUMO-PglC variants retain native-like reentrant topologies, the S23A variant exhibits near-wild type activity, whereas the P24A and S23A/P24A variants are inactive (Figure 9).
evidence: This is demonstrated by activity assays shown in Figure 9.

claim: Pro24 plays a crucial role in mediating polyprenol binding.
source: This suggests that in addition to contributing to RMH formation, Pro24 in particular plays a crucial role in mediating polyprenol binding.
evidence: This is inferred from the loss of activity in P24A mutant despite proper topology.

claim: The Lys-Arg and Ser-Pro motifs enable function by positioning Pro24 to recognize polyprenol phosphate and encourage binding in a catalytically-relevant configuration relative to the PglC active site.
source: Thus, in contributing to formation and stabilization of the RMH, the Lys-Arg and Ser-Pro motifs may enable function by positioning Pro24 to recognize polyprenol phosphate and encourage binding in a catalytically-relevant configuration relative to the PglC active site.
evidence: This is a mechanistic model inferred from structural and functional data.

claim: The proposed model for RMH formation in PglC builds on existing principles of membrane protein topogenesis including the positive-inside rule and peptide backbone hydrogen bonding.
source: The proposed model for RMH formation in PglC (Figure 8) builds on existing principles of membrane protein topogenesis; both the conserved positive charges of the Lys-Arg motif and the helix-breaking 'staple' of the Ser-Pro motif agree well with published observation of the positive-inside rule (Gafvelin and von Heijne, 1994; Heijne, 1986; von Heijne, 2006) and peptide backbone hydrogen bonding (Cymer et al., 2015; Mackenzie, 2006) as driving forces for folding and topology determination of membrane proteins.
evidence: This connects the findings to established principles with citations.

claim: Bitopic membrane proteins constitute 15–25% of all integral membrane proteins in bacteria.
source: Whereas few reentrant monotopic topologies have been structurally characterized to date, topology predications have suggested that bitopic membrane proteins constitute 15–25% of all integral membrane proteins bacteria and are even more prevalent among eukaryotes, accounting for almost half of all human membrane proteins (Almén et al., 2009; Krogh et al., 2001).
evidence: This is based on topology predictions from cited literature.

claim: Bitopic membrane proteins account for almost half of all human membrane proteins.
source: Whereas few reentrant monotopic topologies have been structurally characterized to date, topology predications have suggested that bitopic membrane proteins constitute 15–25% of all integral membrane proteins bacteria and are even more prevalent among eukaryotes, accounting for almost half of all human membrane proteins (Almén et al., 2009; Krogh et al., 2001).
evidence: This is based on topology predictions from cited literature.

claim: The presence of positively-charged residues preceding, and helix-disrupting residues throughout, the hydrophobic domain appears to bias towards a reentrant topology.
source: The presence of positively-charged residues preceding, and helix-disrupting residues throughout, the hydrophobic domain appears to bias towards a reentrant topology.
evidence: This is a generalization based on the findings from PglC and LpxM.

claim: Covariance analysis can be an invaluable tool for topology prediction as it has the capacity to identify interactions between residue pairs that strongly support a reentrant topology.
source: Covariance analysis can additionally be an invaluable tool for topology prediction, as it has the capacity to identify interactions between residue pairs that strongly support a reentrant topology.
evidence: This is based on the successful application of covariance analysis in this study.
